=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Draft SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

**Scope note:** This is a first-pass commercial and legal issues review based only on the Seller's cover note, Seller Update, and Disclosure Letter. I haven't seen the full SPA or the data room. Statutory references are my understanding and should be verified by NSW-qualified counsel before you rely on them.

## Bottom line

The package is not a fair and balanced draft from the Buyer's side. It shifts almost all known risk to the Buyer, and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms that several of those risks are unresolved. Under the proposed drafting, the Buyer would carry the Bluefen consent failure, the Riverlark debt, the Ironquay IP exposure, the undisclosed bonuses, the privacy incident, and the Sandbar costs. Several provisions would also bar claims the Buyer has already identified. I recommend rejecting the package as drafted and marking it up.

## 1. Known issues the Seller's own disclosure confirms

These should be addressed through price, conditions, or specific indemnities, not general warranties.

| # | Issue | Seller position | Problem for Buyer |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Bluefen** (~30% of FY26 revenue, ~AUD 3.6m) | Consent "treated as satisfied" on delivery; reasonable endeavours only. Disclosure says no final consent and no evidence of conditions met. | Loss of the largest customer is possible at Completion. The Seller would carry no risk. |
| 2 | **Riverlark** (~AUD 3.2m debt) | Release "to be provided following Completion." | Debt-free/cash-free means debt must be repaid from price at Completion. A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer funding the Seller's debt and the Company's security in place. |
| 3 | **Ironquay IP** (AUD 180k open on SOW3; transfer conditional on payment) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment, "considered adequate." | Ownership of Project Materials is unconfirmed. Exposure extends beyond the fee to ownership and third-party claims. |
| 4 | **Employee bonuses** (AUD 420k) | "a matter for the Seller," not in funds flow. | Completion bonuses are a debt-like item. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are unquantified. If left out, the Buyer pays them. |
| 5 | **Privacy/export incident** (~1,240 records: names, business emails, roles, timestamps) | Described as "preliminary," not a confirmed breach, no loss amount. | Business email addresses and activity data are likely personal information. If the incident is an eligible data breach under Part IIIC of the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), the Company must assess it promptly and notify if required. That clock may already be running, and the Company, which the Buyer will own, would be the entity responsible. |
| 6 | **Sandbar renewals** (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs." | Disclosure says it does not confirm whether they are unavoidable, terminable, or accrued. The "ordinary course" label is unsupported and inconsistent with the disclosure. |
| 7 | **Office lease** | Notification obligation only. | Landlord consent to a change of control has not been excluded. |
| 8 | **Mossvale** | Assignment restriction. | Consent for a share sale has not been excluded. |
| 9 | **Title** (100% shares) | Relies on share register at DD-012. | The register shows the Seller, but the Buyer needs independent verification (ASIC extract, encumbrance searches, options). |

**Quantified known items, before on-costs and Bluefen:** Riverlark AUD 3.2m + bonuses AUD 420k + Ironquay AUD 180k + Sandbar AUD 330k ≈ **AUD 4.13m**. Riverlark is a price deduction, not a claim, but the total shows the scale of the known exposure against a 20% cap of AUD 4.8m, which is already largely consumed by known matters if they fall under warranties.

## 2. Structural provisions that gut the Buyer's protection

**a) Buyer knowledge clause (8.3).** This is an anti-sandbagging clause. Given the Buyer's diligence, it would exclude claims on nearly every known issue above, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records." Reject it. Propose an express pro-sandbagging clause, since NSW law on buyer knowledge is not settled and an express term is needed.

**b) General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2, Schedule 7).** Disclosing "every fact" in the data room is effectively a blanket exception to all warranties. Reject it. Disclosure should be specific, fair, and fairly disclosed in a way that identifies the matter. Also note the data room is frozen at 22 September 2026, while today is 5 November 2026. Require a bring-down disclosure and a Completion-date data room refresh.

**c) Non-reliance, exclusive-remedy and limitation provisions applied to "all Claims of any nature" (9.3, 12.8, 20.5).** Fraud must be carved out expressly, and the clause should not limit claims for fraud or wilful concealment. Consider also whether these provisions can exclude misleading or deceptive conduct claims under the Australian Consumer Law. Check the enforceability position with counsel.

**d) Market-context assertions.** The cover note's claims about "standard" caps, baskets, and time limits are not authority. Ask the Seller for supporting precedent or drop them. The statement that terms were "settled at principal level" and are "not intended to be re-opened" does not bind the Buyer unless signed terms exist. Check whether any signed heads of agreement or exclusivity letter contains binding positions. Do not accept the "FINAL" label as a reason to stop negotiating.

## 3. Liability and thresholds

- **General cap (12.1), 20% / AUD 4.8m:** Already at the top of the Seller's own range and not enough given the known exposures. Push for a higher cap (the Buyer should decide the number, but a figure closer to 30% or more is a reasonable opening). Carve out fundamental warranties, tax, and specific indemnities from the cap.
- **De minimis AUD 25k and basket AUD 250k with excess-only recovery (12.2):** The basket is about 1% of price and operates as a deductible. Push for a **tipping basket** (first-dollar recovery once exceeded), a lower de minimis (e.g., AUD 10k, with aggregation of related claims), and exclusion of known matters from threshold calculations.

## 4. Time limits

- **18-month general claims period:** Short for a SaaS business with IP and privacy exposure. Push for at least 24–36 months for general warranties, given audit cycles.
- **"Any limitation applies to all Claims" (13):** This pulls fundamental and tax claims into the 18-month window. Reject. Under the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW), contract claims generally run six years and deed claims longer. Consider executing the SPA as a deed and check the exact period. Tax claims should run to the statutory assessment period plus a buffer.

## 5. Fundamental and title warranties

The proposal to subject capacity and title warranties to the general cap and time limits is unacceptable. Title and capacity should:
- be capped at 100% of price (or the Buyer's chosen figure);
- run for at least six years, or longer if the SPA is a deed;
- sit outside the basket and de minimis.

## 6. Conditions and completion mechanics

- **Bluefen:** Make written Bluefen consent, with conditions under 11.3 satisfied, an express condition precedent that the Buyer can waive. Reject "treat as satisfied on delivery," as that is a Seller-favourable reinterpretation. If consent is not obtained, the Buyer needs a price adjustment, escrow, or a right to walk away. Upgrade "reasonable endeavours" to "all reasonable endeavours," with costs borne by the Seller.
- **Riverlark:** Require a payoff letter and discharge of security (including PPSR discharge) delivered at Completion. Repay from the price in the funds flow. A post-Completion release is not acceptable.
- **Funds flow:** Add the bonuses as a debt-like item with on-costs, and confirm the Riverlark repayment and any Sandbar costs in the price calculation. The cover note's statement that the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" is not verified by the disclosure.

## 7. Specific indemnities and security

Propose specific indemnities, outside basket and cap (subject to negotiation), for:
1. **Bluefen:** loss of revenue or contract termination arising from change-of-control consent.
2. **Ironquay:** all SOW fees, IP ownership of Project Materials, and third-party claims. Require a confirmatory assignment as a condition.
3. **Privacy incident:** investigation, notification, regulatory penalties to the extent insurable, customer claims, and remediation costs.
4. **Employee bonuses and on-costs.**
5. **Pre-Completion tax**, including on tax and IP warranties the Seller has called "settled."
6. **Sandbar renewals**, unless they are shown to be ordinary-course and not accelerated by the sale.
7. **Lease and Mossvale consents**, if required.

Support these with an **escrow or retention** sized to the quantified exposure, with a release mechanism tied to Bluefen and the incident outcome.

## 8. Tax and IP warranties

The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not. Require full tax warranties (including a pre-Completion tax indemnity) and IP warranties covering ownership, contractor assignments, open source, and no infringement. The Ironquay position shows why this matters.

## 9. Immediate information requests

1. Current status of the privacy assessment under Part IIIC, including any 30-day assessment deadline and whether notification has been made.
2. Bluefen consent correspondence and the conditions under clause 11.3.
3. Riverlark payoff letter and discharge plan.
4. Ironquay payment records, SOW3 Project Materials, and any ownership claims.
5. Bonus schedule with on-cost calculations and employment conditions.
6. Sandbar contract terms, termination rights, and renewal dates.
7. Lease and Mossvale change-of-control provisions.
8. ASIC extract, share transfer documents, and PPSR search for title and encumbrances.
9. Any signed term sheet, heads of agreement, or exclusivity letter supporting the "FINAL" claim.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the package as drafted** and send a full mark-up. Make clear the "FINAL" label does not stop negotiation unless binding terms were signed.
2. **Remove or narrow the buyer-knowledge clause (8.3)** and insert an express pro-sandbagging clause.
3. **Limit general disclosure** to specific disclosure, and require a bring-down and data-room refresh to Completion.
4. **Carve out fraud** from non-reliance, exclusive-remedy, and limitation provisions.
5. **Raise the general cap** and carve out fundamental, tax, and specific indemnities.
6. **Move to a tipping basket** with a lower de minimis, and exclude known matters from thresholds.
7. **Extend general claims to 24–36 months**, and set fundamental and tax claims to statutory periods.
8. **Cap title and capacity at 100% of price** with six-year or longer claims periods, outside basket and de minimis.
9. **Make Bluefen consent a condition precedent**, with a price adjustment or walk-away right if not obtained.
10. **Require a payoff letter and security discharge for Riverlark at Completion**, repaid from the price.
11. **Add the AUD 420k bonuses and on-costs as debt-like items** in the funds flow.
12. **Expand the Ironquay indemnity** beyond the SOW3 fee to cover IP ownership and third-party claims.
13. **Obtain specific indemnities** for the privacy incident, pre-Completion tax, Sandbar costs, and any landlord or Mossvale consents.
14. **Establish escrow or retention** sized to quantified exposure (~AUD 4.1m before on-costs and Bluefen), released against Bluefen and incident outcomes.
15. **Upgrade tax and IP warranties** and require the Seller to justify "settled" positions.
16. **Verify title independently** via ASIC extract, share transfer documents, and PPSR search.
17. **Ask the Seller to support its market-context claims** with evidence, or withdraw them.

Next steps: confirm the Buyer's target cap and escrow figures, and have NSW-qualified M&A and privacy counsel review the mark-up, particularly the limitation, deed execution, ACL, and Privacy Act points.
